name: American Tower Corporation

profile.description: American Tower Corporation is a global communications-infrastructure REIT owning and operating wireless and broadcast towers across the U.S., Latin America, Europe and Africa, plus a fast-growing interconnection-focused data center business through its CoreSite subsidiary. Q3 2026 (reported October 27, 2026) total revenue rose 2.5% to $2.785B, property revenue grew 4.5% to $2.734B, organic tenant billings growth slowed to 1.1%, and data center cash revenue grew 16.3%. AFFO per share was $2.87 (+3.2%) and full-year AFFO/share guidance was nudged up to $11.04-$11.16, while the board expanded the buyback program by $2B. CEO Steven Vondran leads the company.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): The 2021 CoreSite acquisition opened a genuinely new revenue engine — data center cash revenue grew 16.3% in Q3 2026 while U.S. tower organic billings growth slowed to 1.1%, and management says CoreSite capacity has been expanded ~1.5x since the deal with demand still exceeding supply [1][2]. AI Deployment (1/2): Vondran describes AI inferencing, ML training and GPU-as-a-service as a fast-growing component of CoreSite leasing, but internal AI cost-savings efforts in the tower business are described as 'early stage' with no quantified savings [2]. Market Share (2/2): One of the three dominant U.S. tower owners with a global footprint spanning the Americas, Europe and Africa, and CoreSite is a leading interconnection hub for cloud and network customers [2][5]. Product Pipeline (1/2): Data center capacity expansions and 5G densification provide visibility, and FY2026 property revenue guidance of $10.785-$10.865B is specific, but there is no named next-generation product with launch dates [1]. R&D Intensity (0/1): Reported R&D expense is $0 — innovation happens through capex, not research [4].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): American Tower's stated purpose of building and operating the infrastructure that connects people and businesses is clear and has real societal reach in emerging markets, but it is framed as a business proposition and is largely interchangeable with peers Crown Castle and SBA [5]. Community Impact (1/2): The company publishes sustainability reporting with board-level oversight by the Nominating Committee and carries low ESG-risk ratings (Sustainalytics 12.6), plus digital-inclusion programs in its emerging-market footprint, but no distinctive, dollar-quantified community program surfaced [5]. Employee Retention (0/2): Reported headcount is 4,866 versus roughly 6,200 previously cited, consistent with portfolio divestitures and efficiency programs rather than evidence of above-average retention [3]. Insider Buying (0/2): No meaningful net insider buying was identified in the last 12 months.

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on dividend-stock metrics (12 weight units). D/E of 463.8% scores 0.0 (above the 300% floor) [3]. ROE of 33.0% scores 1.0 and profit margin of 30.1% scores 1.0 [3]. Revenue growth YoY of 2.5% scores 0.75, consistent with Q3 2026 total revenue +2.5% [1][3]. 5-year revenue CAGR of 5.8% (FY2020 $8.04B to FY2025 $10.65B, derived from reported income statements) scores 0.72 [4]. Forward P/E of 26.9 scores 0.83 [3]. Payout ratio of 99.6% (GAAP basis; REITs distribute on AFFO) scores 0.01 [3]. Dividends paid every year since 2012 (15 years) score 1.0 at 2x weight; annual dividend totals rose every year 2012-2025 (14 years) score 1.0; 5-year dividend CAGR of ~8.5% ($4.53 in 2020 to $6.80 in 2025, derived from Yahoo dividend history) scores 1.0 at 2x weight [6]. Weighted sum 9.30 / 12 x 10 = 7.75, rounds to 8. Liquidity: $188.30 x 2.80M shares = ~$528M daily — far above the $1M floor.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (7/9): Physical tower sites with long-term carrier leases cannot be substituted by software, and AI workloads add demand for both wireless densification and the interconnection-dense data centers CoreSite operates [2]. The searches surfaced no analyst commentary flagging AI as a substitution risk to towers; the nearest demand risk is hyperscaler lease rationalization in data centers (a 2024 TD Cowen channel check), plus slowing U.S. tower organic growth (1.1% in Q3 2026) which is carrier-driven rather than AI-driven [1][2]. Points are held below 'immune' because the U.S. tower business is decelerating and data center demand is concentrated among a few large AI/cloud buyers. AI Opportunity (1/1): CoreSite data center cash revenue grew 16.3% in Q3 2026, and management explicitly identifies AI inferencing, ML and GPU-as-a-service as a fast-growing share of new leases [1][2].

infinite_game.summary: American Tower plays a long-duration game: multi-decade tower leases, a dividend that has risen every year since the 2012 REIT conversion, and a strategic pivot into data centers ahead of the tower slowdown [1][6]. By Sinek's lens it scores 7/10 — strong existential flexibility (CoreSite) and constructive rivalry with Crown Castle, SBA and Equinix, but a cause that reads as commercial rather than idealistic and a Q3 2026 capital-allocation emphasis on a $2B buyback expansion that favors per-share optics.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): Connecting people and businesses through shared infrastructure is resilient and service-oriented, and it extends credibly from towers into data centers as connectivity demand moves to compute [2][5]. It falls short of a 3 because leadership communicates it primarily in growth and AFFO terms rather than as an idealistic future state, and it is not distinctive versus tower peers.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): The organization operates a large global portfolio with a lean team and has integrated CoreSite without visible disruption, with long-serving executives such as CoreSite CEO Juan Font (25+ years in data centers/telecom) [2]. Headcount has nonetheless fallen to 4,866 from roughly 6,200, and no employee-engagement or tenure data surfaced to justify a 2 [3].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (1/1): AMT positions CoreSite as an interconnection hub rather than a pure capacity play, a deliberate differentiation from Equinix and Digital Realty, and competes in towers within a rational three-player market alongside Crown Castle and SBA where shared-infrastructure economics reward co-existence rather than destruction [2].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (2/2): The CoreSite acquisition was a genuine reinvention ahead of the tower slowdown — in Q3 2026 data center cash revenue grew 16.3% while U.S. tower organic billings growth fell to 1.1%, validating the pivot [1][2]. Exiting India and reshaping the international portfolio further shows willingness to let go of legacy assets [4].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Paying a premium for CoreSite in 2021 despite investor skepticism, and continuing to fund capacity expansion, was a costly long-term bet that is now paying off [2]. However, Q3 2026 AFFO-per-share upside was attributed largely to capital allocation and the board expanded the buyback by $2B — a financial-engineering lever Sinek would view as finite-game behavior when U.S. organic growth is slowing [1].

investment_thesis: American Tower is a scaled digital-infrastructure REIT whose growth engine has shifted from towers to data centers. Q3 2026 revenue of $2.785B (+2.5%) beat consensus, AFFO per share rose 3.2% to $2.87, data center cash revenue grew 16.3%, and full-year AFFO/share guidance was raised to $11.04-$11.16 [1]. CoreSite capacity is up ~1.5x since acquisition with demand still exceeding supply, and management cites AI inferencing and GPU-as-a-service as fast-growing lease categories [2]. Profitability is excellent — ROE 33.0% and profit margin 30.1% — and the 3.8% yield is backed by 14 consecutive years of dividend growth and an ~8.5% 5-year dividend CAGR [3][6]. The stock at $188.30 has rallied above its 50-day average of $175, and the newly expanded $2B buyback adds per-share support [1][3].
thesis_continued: The bear case is a decelerating core and a stretched balance sheet. U.S. tower organic tenant billings growth slowed to just 1.1% in Q3 2026 and net income fell 14.4%, with full-year net income guidance cut to $3.25-$3.31B on unrealized equity losses [1]. D/E of 463.8% and a GAAP payout ratio near 100% leave little cushion if rates stay high or AFFO disappoints, and a forward P/E of 26.9x already prices CoreSite strength [3]. Data center demand is concentrated among a handful of hyperscalers, and earlier channel checks showed hyperscalers can terminate leases with private operators [2]. The Inspire Impact Score of -49 (MISALIGNED) also limits suitability for faith-based mandates despite broad positive ESG attributions.
key_catalysts: CoreSite data center cash revenue growth sustaining mid-teens (16.3% in Q3 2026) as AI inference and GPU-as-a-service leasing scale, with capacity additions converting existing excess demand into revenue [1][2]
Execution of the $2B buyback expansion announced October 2026 lifting AFFO per share toward the top of the $11.04-$11.16 FY2026 range [1]
Re-acceleration of U.S. tower organic billings growth from 1.1% as carrier 5G densification spending resumes and churn headwinds roll off [1]
key_risks: U.S. tower organic tenant billings growth of only 1.1% in Q3 2026 signals a mature core that may not support a 26.9x forward P/E if data center growth slows [1][3]
Leverage (D/E 463.8%) and a ~100% GAAP payout ratio make the dividend and valuation sensitive to higher-for-longer interest rates and refinancing costs [3]
Customer concentration in data centers — hyperscaler lease terminations at private operators (per 2024 channel checks) show AI-driven demand can reverse quickly [2]
